title: Palindrome check
prompt:
Write `is_palindrome` for a piece of text: it is `true` when the text reads the same forwards and backwards, otherwise `false`. Treat upper and lower case as different letters (no need to handle spaces).

```text
is_palindrome("racecar") -> true
is_palindrome("hello")   -> false
is_palindrome("a")       -> true
```

Signature: `bool is_palindrome(const char *s)`
hints: Compare the first character with the last, the second with the second-to-last, and so on.
Two index variables, one at the start and one at the end, moving towards each other, do the job. Stop when they meet.
Or: build the reversed text and compare it with the original.
`strlen(s)` is unsigned; cast it with `(int)strlen(s)` before subtracting 1.
explanation: A palindrome equals its own reverse. Comparing from both ends toward the middle avoids building a second copy of the text.
